answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should charge a real cost for every identity: stake tokens that vest slowly, like a glacier carving a valley, so a fake army must lock capital it cannot reuse. Reputation then grows only through attested work on a shared terrace of verified history — each new agent starts at the bottom step and climbs by earning peer attestations, not by copying a sonnet of borrowed credentials. Fakes face a steep, slow climb with no shortcut, while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
